newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislative panel to review school funding.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislative panel to review school funding.

text.p: California's state legislative leaders said Thursday they formed a special committee of lawmakers to develop a long-term plan to finance the state's school construction needs.
By some accounts, $30 billion is needed statewide to improve schools.

State Assembly Speaker Cruz Bustamante and Senate President Pro Tem Bill Lockyer, both Democrats, said the panel would develop financing plans to reduce class sizes, address student enrollment growth, and repair older facilities.
Lockyer added in a statement: "We are looking to the special committee to spend its time finding breakthrough answers to these long-standing problems."
Education leaders said the special committee could help address the state's school funding needs.

"The facilities issue is reaching crisis proportions," said Mamie Starr, president of the statewide Coalition for Adequate School Housing. "There are a number of issues related to solving the problem that need legislative attention."
Starr estimated that there is a $30 billion school housing need statewide.
